tldr: For every fixed known propensity \(e\) satisfying \(c_-x^{5/2}\le e(x)\le c_+x^{5/2}\), the minimax absolute risk and uniformly \(95\%\)-honest connected-interval maximal expected length are both \(n^{-2/5}\{\log(en)\}^{2/5}\) on each of \(\mathcal F\) and \(\mathcal F_0\), with constants common over the entire comparability class. The same observable estimator and computable interval family witness all fixed-design upper bounds simultaneously, so the uniform known-design class criteria have the identical rate. The proved chain is \(\mathtt{thm{:}joint\mbox{-}jackson\mbox{-}factorial\mbox{-}certificate}\longrightarrow\mathtt{thm{:}observable\mbox{-}upper}\longrightarrow\mathtt{thm{:}fixed\mbox{-}design\mbox{-}four\mbox{-}criterion\mbox{-}frontier}\longrightarrow\mathtt{thm{:}four\mbox{-}criterion\mbox{-}frontier}\).
